# Migrate existing work

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_guides.py; edit src/, then regenerate. -->

This document contains the complete route, story template and execution rules. Start with the route, working agreement and copyable story. Apply the access, execution, review and publication rules relevant to the work before taking those actions. Examples and review history are optional.

Use one guide commit: record a commit-pinned link's SHA; otherwise resolve the supplied branch/tag once and read this document at that SHA. Reuse content already fully present and verified at the same SHA; reread only if changed, truncated or provenance is uncertain. API clients must pass the SHA explicitly. Record this document path, SHA and route in the story. Refresh deliberately and reconcile changed rules; never mix revisions.

If required content is missing, inaccessible or incomplete, report it and stop dependent work; do not guess or silently substitute an older copy. Continue independent authorized work only when the gap cannot invalidate it. This guide grants no authority to build, deploy, spend, share externally or change criteria. A link supplies neither inaccessible chat history nor permission. Infer inputs and existing authority from available context; ask only for unresolved information needed for the next action.

## Route

1. Inventory the latest story, comments, criteria, decisions, design, research, code and evidence. Confirm source revisions, destination repository/folder, branch, concurrent work and existing authorization. Keep a compact source revision → destination/reference → disposition map for material artifacts, decisions, evidence and links in the existing history or execution record linked from the story. Use opaque references for restricted sources. Read relevant prior chats only where they resolve gaps. Distinguish observed results, historical reports, proposals and model opinions; another project’s state is not this project’s evidence.
2. Capture the current ClickUp description verbatim as historical evidence before replacing it. Keep client-identifying originals in approved restricted storage, with an access-controlled mapping to sanitized parameters. Preserve existing attachments and material history. Do not move private content into public Git history.
3. Populate the Copyable story template from the inventory. Preserve agreed criterion IDs and wording, decisions and useful artifact links. Compare source and destination criteria and classify every difference, including sanitization. A missing, inaccessible or unauthorized alteration to a required criterion blocks migration completion. Do not invent evidence, approvals, names, URLs or model identities. Reconcile conflicting facts rather than overwrite them.
4. Reconcile each step against evidence. Keep valid completed work complete; do not restart it merely because the format changed. Reopen checks affected by changed inputs or criteria and leave unverified results NOT RUN. Retain previous execution records, blockers, fixes and review dispositions. Select the next eligible step using the Executors and bounded execution rules.
5. Apply the Privacy, publication and links rules for publication checks. Read back the published revision and verify access to the folder, story and required evidence. Confirm authority to edit the ClickUp item; refresh its text/comments immediately before writeback and reconcile intervening changes. Replace the current description with the story's Outcome sentence, copied verbatim, and one direct link to the current GitHub story file; retain the short title/ID, applicable grouping/filtering fields and synchronized owner/date/status fields from their authoritative sources. Read back the result. Preserve originals; mark prior current locations historical or superseded only after the new link and required access work for the intended reader. Keep a recoverable prior reference if the transition fails, and do not maintain two competing current stories.
6. Record the migration revision, source references, differences, preservation checks, unresolved gaps and next action in the linked history or execution record. Reconcile current-state, next-action, configuration and decision statements across retained documents against their authoritative sources. Verify required restricted-context retrieval before claiming portability; record unresolved map/access gaps. Execute only remaining work already authorized. A migration does not transfer prior client permissions, fixture reservations or acceptance to a new environment. Failed synchronization remains an explicit blocker, not a claimed success.

For mixed work, migrate existing scope first. Put genuinely new scope in a separate linked story unless existing user authority permits extending the original criteria; record authorized extensions as material changes with affected checks. For a new story, check for existing related work before creating a duplicate; use the Copyable story template, define stable observable criteria, preserve agreed brief requirements and label new interpretations as proposals; establish outcome, scope and exclusions, then record the next eligible action using the shared rules. Use MIGRATE+NEW only for an authorized extension within one story. Otherwise record MIGRATE on the migrated story and NEW on the linked new story, each with this guide path and SHA and a link to the other. Retain both scopes clearly. Confirm the destination and authority before creating any repository or ClickUp item; stop only unresolved dependent writes. Do not reread the new-work guide merely for mixed scope.

## Working agreement

Refresh the current story, relevant comments, decisions, dependencies, evidence and authority. When delegating an external change to another chat or agent, include a retrievable reference to the originating human instruction, the authorized action/destination and any visibility assumption. The receiving executor verifies that source; a handoff is not new authority. Keep private authorization references restricted. Reuse accurate work; distinguish facts, historical reports, proposals and reviewer opinions. Never invent identities, results, approvals, URLs or implementation. Keep agreed criterion IDs and wording; material changes need reasons, applicable authority and affected rechecks.

When upgrading an existing story to a newer guide, record both guide commit SHAs, compare changed rules and map affected checks. Preserve prior results as historical; retain still-valid evidence, reopen affected checks, and mark checks not yet performed NOT RUN. Do not silently rewrite the guide provenance or restart completed work.

ClickUp holds the short story title/ID, epic or parent grouping, ownership, dates, status and applicable priority, categories, flags and labels for filtering and understanding the work. Its description contains only the story's Outcome sentence, copied verbatim from the published story, and one direct link to the current GitHub story file. Keep requirements, acceptance criteria, solution/design, execution checklists, research and QA evidence in GitHub and reference them by link when needed. Keep filtering fields concise; avoid copying delivery content into custom fields or comments. Preserve historical source snapshots under the migration rules. GitHub holds the detailed record. Execution evidence governs delivery status; cited human decisions or designated assignment fields govern ownership. Reconcile conflicts and keep unresolved ones visible. Do not maintain competing current stories; preserve historical snapshots.

Use relevant official platform documentation and identify the supported claim and source section/version. Verify actual target metadata, edition, API version, access and behavior before relying on it. A URL proves neither compatibility nor runtime success. A new client/laptop supplies its own configuration and evidence: permissions, acceptance and fixture reservations do not automatically transfer.

## Privacy, publication and links

Keep client identities, instance URLs, real records, credentials and restricted evidence outside public Git. When sanitizing, preserve meaning with named parameters and a restricted mapping; compare source and published criteria and classify every difference. Missing or unauthorized changes to agreed criteria block completion. Use placeholders/synthetic data and an approved restricted index with opaque references, access owner and retrieval instructions. Keep restricted originals and the mapping outside the repository in an approved access-controlled location; the index identifies its access owner and retrieval procedure without exposing sensitive paths publicly. Ignored local/private/reviews paths are only an accidental-add safety net, not approved private storage by themselves. Do not invent public chat links. Missing or inaccessible required evidence remains a gap. Before claiming a portable handoff, verify that the intended authorized executor can retrieve required restricted context using the recorded access owner and mechanism; a pointer to one laptop is not enough.

Before publishing, inspect files/diff, names, commit/branch text, author metadata and history for unauthorized disclosure. `.gitignore` does not remove tracked content or history. Do not falsify author identity. Coordinate the branch, preserve concurrent edits, publish only to the authorized repository and read back saved content and links. Report synchronization failures with a durable local record; never claim success without readback.

Use mutable links for current story/folder and immutable commit/blob references for reviewed inputs and evidence. Label draft branches; verify access as the intended reader. Before replacing any existing ClickUp description, confirm edit authority and capture its current text verbatim (restricted if client-identifying). Account for its criteria in the source/destination comparison. Refresh immediately before writing and reconcile intervening edits. If refreshed text differs from the capture, preserve the refreshed text verbatim and compare/classify its criteria before replacement; replace only after the GitHub files/links are verified, then read back the saved description and fields. Do not use description length or perceived importance to skip preservation.

If the ClickUp item or access is missing, record synchronization as Pending with the reason and needed item/access/authority; request missing information once and retain the gap until resolved. Do not invent an item or create one without authority. Continue independent authorized GitHub work and report its publication separately; do not claim ClickUp synchronization or overall completion while a required sync remains unresolved.

## Copyable story

```markdown

**Owner** · <Confirmed story owner or Pending confirmation> · [Story and execution record](<revision-pinned link>) · [Guide](<revision-pinned link>)

**Outcome** · As <actor>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

**Demo result** · <Date, scenario, identity verified or unverified, and observed result. If nothing ran, write NOT RUN.> [Evidence](<revision-pinned link>)

**Acceptance** · <What remains open and what was outside scope. If closure was directed, state who authorized it and exactly what they closed.> [Decision, if recorded](<revision-pinned link>)

## Proposed scenario checks
<Include when the story is driven by proposed test scenarios. Include the setup bullets for demo stories.>

- **Where / who** · <Authorized environment and entry link. Sign in as the intended role or test user.>
- **Start with** · <Direct test-record links, required starting state, and safe reset if needed.>

**Demo sequence** · <Presenter check IDs in order. Include only when the list also contains setup or QA checks.>

1. **<Check ID>** · <Actor and action> → <One visible expected outcome for a presenter step, or the observable expectation for a QA check. Include exact values, counts, and record relationships where relevant.> <Applicable criterion IDs>

| Check ID | Status | Observed result and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| <Check ID> | NOT RUN | <When run, record the observed result and link pinned evidence.> |

## Acceptance criteria
<Include for agreed criteria and for proposed criteria that are not already captured in the scenario checks.>

| Criterion ID | Criterion | Coverage and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| <Stable AC ID> | <Preserve original IDs and agreed wording verbatim. Label new, unagreed wording Proposed.> | <Reference applicable check IDs and any coverage gaps, or record the result and pinned evidence here when there is no separate check.> |

## Material blockers
<Use one current entry per distinct material blocker. Reference the affected step or check IDs.>

**<Step/check IDs> · <Short status>**
- **Goal** · <What must the actor accomplish?>
- **Blocker** · <What prevents it?>
- **Current fix** · <Smallest proposed fix, or verified fix with evidence link>
- **Documentation** · <One best documentation URL. Omit if unavailable.>

## Admin guidance
<Optional at closeout for settings an admin will maintain. Use one bullet per material change.>

- **<What to change>** · <Exact verified admin UI path or durable link to verified runbook instructions> · Replay <existing check ID>. <Include a verified prerequisite or activation step only if it affects the change.>

**Next** · <One action tied to an existing step or human decision and the relevant criterion or check IDs. If assignment is pending, name who can assign the verifier or write Pending confirmation. Otherwise name the confirmed executor.> · <Prerequisites> · [Existing step or decision](<revision-pinned link>)
```

## Keep the story reviewable

Lead with the story’s outcome. Put acceptance criteria in a clearly labeled section. Group related criteria and give each distinct condition its own bullet. Place safeguards and exceptions beside the criteria they qualify. Link or cite evidence where it applies, and include the context a reviewer needs to interpret it.

For new stories, write criteria directly and preserve any wording required verbatim. For migrated stories, carry forward required verbatim criteria exactly as written. Put clarifications in a separate note so reviewers can distinguish them from the source wording.

Stories have no word limit. During review, remove repeated explanations and move optional background to a linked reference. Keep every required criterion, safeguard, exception, and detail needed to judge acceptance in the story itself.

Give each proposed check a stable ID. State the actor, action, and observable expectation once, including exact values, counts, and record relationships where relevant. For platform checks, also state the exact read or observation that produces the result. Where evidence is absent, record Pending with the reason; where sources conflict, record both and do not record Pass until the conflict is reconciled. Preserve agreed criteria verbatim. Map checks to criteria by ID in either direction as needed. Track status, observed result, and evidence by check ID. Use `NOT RUN` until execution.

Use only the sections that apply. For a proposed scenario, the scenario bullets carry the proposed expectations. The results table tracks outcomes and evidence by ID. Retain agreed criterion IDs and exact wording in the acceptance criteria section and use references to show coverage and gaps. For new work without a scenario, label unagreed criteria Proposed in that section.

## Using the story

Draft the demo in the story as soon as the path is known. Mark pending fixtures or access explicitly. Write each presenter action once, in replay order, using its stable check ID. Keep QA queries in the QA record and track observed results and evidence by ID.

Revise the setup and actions in place as you run them. Before marking the story demo-ready, confirm intended-user access and record links, verify the safe reset, and replay the sequence from the stated starting condition. Restore the starting state afterward where a safe, authorized reset applies. Omit credentials. Keep restricted links in an authorized record and use a safe reference in the story.

Capture candidate admin paths during execution. Verify them as the intended admin, including any required activation sequence. Finalize Admin guidance after the relevant acceptance checks pass and before closing the story. A passing buyer demo verifies buyer behavior only. Keep proposed admin paths in the execution record until verified, and reference existing checks by ID so the buyer demo stays intact.

Record one next action, its owner, and the agreed criterion it advances or the decision a named human needs to make. Label proposals explicitly. Only an authorized decision changes agreed scope or criteria. Report what was observed, with a reference to the evidence. Keep commands, logs, test steps, and repair history in linked execution or QA files. At closeout, add a **Files** index. Link each file and describe its purpose in at most eight words.

Start with known checks. Refine Next as fixture, user, permission, documentation, or smaller-step needs emerge. Use plain language and fewer than 30 words each for Goal, Blocker, and Current fix. Mark a proposed fix unverified until tested.

Try the smallest authorized fix first and verify it against the blocker. If stuck, send one authorized reviewer the same three fields, the documentation URL if available, and only essential sanitized evidence in a reusable thread. Request at most 60 words covering one actionable next step, its success check, and any approval or access needed.

The execution agent validates advice, retries only with new evidence or a changed hypothesis, and escalates access or approval needs. Update Current fix in place after failures. On resolution, retain only the verified fix there and link evidence. Preserve prior criteria and evidence. Record material side effects, decisions, and mandatory evidence in existing QA records.

Use the existing execution or QA record when it has the needed detail. Check the Files index against tracked story files, including subfolders, and verify its links before closing. Keep any required independent verification and human acceptance explicit.

### Example: Quantity rules and volume pricing

- **Where / who** · Open the demo storefront as the test buyer.
- **Start with** · Open the gauze-box product. Confirm the isolated cart is empty. For a safe reset, remove only the demo line when authorized.

**Demo sequence** · AC-03 → AC-04 → AC-05 → AC-06

1. **AC-03** · Add 8 boxes → $80 subtotal.
2. **AC-04** · Try 9 boxes → rejected. The cart stays at 8 boxes and $80.
3. **AC-05** · Enter 10 boxes → $9 each, $90 subtotal.
4. **AC-06** · Enter 12 boxes → $9 each, $108 subtotal.

**AC-03 · Resolved**

- **Goal** · Add eight units as the test buyer and verify one cart line at $80.
- **Blocker** · The buyer page showed Out of Stock. In-app browser control then became unavailable.
- **Current fix** · Playwright Chrome restored buyer testing. Add To Cart was enabled, and AC-03 passed. [Verification details](https://github.com/aispanda/B2B-Commerce/blob/5b5d8838cfbdc2a8075e368b024b28a1a4501ed7/epics/e01-customer-ordering/stories/purchase-quantity-rules-and-volume-pricing/story.md#verification-details)
- **Documentation** · [Omnichannel Inventory Connect REST APIs](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=commerce.inv_omnichannel_inventory_connect_rest_apis.htm&language=en_US&type=5)

[Full example and results](https://github.com/aispanda/B2B-Commerce/blob/5b5d8838cfbdc2a8075e368b024b28a1a4501ed7/epics/e01-customer-ordering/stories/purchase-quantity-rules-and-volume-pricing/story.md)

## Platform access check

For stories that read or change an external platform, put **Verify platform access** first in the execution plan linked from the story. Make platform discovery, review, build, testing and writes depend on the probe for each tool they use. Keep existing task IDs when adding it to a migrated story.

- **Choose the tools.** Use the approved platform MCP or CLI for backend operations and backend tests. Verify each tool the story will use against the intended account and environment with a minimal read-only probe. Use Playwright or another browser tool for tests of the user journey and user acceptance, acting as the intended user. Browser sign-in also supports tool authentication when needed.
- **Salesforce.** Verify Headless 360 MCP and Salesforce CLI independently against the intended org, each with a minimal authorized read, and record each result separately. Start with MCP: discover, describe, then dispatch_readonly. For CLI, check `sf org list --json` privately and run a read-only API check such as `sf org list limits --target-org <ALIAS> --json`. Use MCP first for org work when its probe passes; otherwise use the verified CLI for the reads it supports and record MCP as unavailable. Writes require existing authority. If a check fails, open only the matching recovery guide at this guide revision: [MCP setup and recovery](../docs/salesforce-mcp.md) or [CLI setup and recovery](../docs/salesforce-cli.md). If both pass, skip the recovery guides.
- **Record the result.** Record the tools, target environment, checks, results and time. Keep private identifiers and credentials in restricted storage. If a required connection fails, record the exact error with sensitive values redacted and block only the steps that need that tool until rechecked. Recheck when the executor environment or authorization changes. Changes to OAuth scopes or security settings require explicit authorization.

- **Map the documentation.** Before deriving detailed checks, read the applicable official product documentation and cite it as the Working agreement requires. In the linked execution record, classify each material behavior as established by a cited source section, not covered by the documentation, or needing actual observation in the target environment, and derive checks from that map. Retain previously accepted results whose inputs and criteria are unchanged. Reading documentation does not wait on access; a missing source or tool holds only the checks that depend on it.
- **Validate the checklist manually.** Before relying on or automating derived checks, run them by hand on one synthetic case already authorized for the story and compare each result with independent evidence. Then run one case with missing or conflicting evidence and confirm the checks report Pending or Fail, not Pass. Record both runs under the affected check IDs in the existing results and blocker sections.

## Executors and bounded execution

Choose the simplest approach that meets the story’s acceptance criteria. Where repetition or consistency warrants it, create or reuse a small template, populate it with automation and AI as appropriate, validate it against source evidence, and generate the deliverable. Keep one authoritative source for each fact and independently verify the finished result. Expand the structure only when its benefit justifies creation, review and maintenance.

One assigned executor per step; split meaningful human/AI/automation handoffs. The accountable human may differ. Unresolved required assignment blocks dispatch.

- **Human:** actual person and action/decision.
- **Automation:** deterministic workflow/script/tool, version, trigger and accountable operator; AI judgment is not automation.
- **AI:** record **Model** and **Reasoning** using the IDE's names. Follow user/project choices and existing system constraints. Otherwise choose the model by task: routine work → economical; implementation → balanced; difficult debugging, analysis or consequential review → more capable. Set reasoning separately to match task difficulty. Prefer task-relevant quality, then cost and speed. Use the model's supported setting, such as Low, Medium, High or Extra high; write Default when the tool manages reasoning, or Auto when it selects the model. Note any selection change in the task result.

Examples, not fixed assignments (checked 13 November 2026): [Meta Muse Wonder](https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-wonder); [Google Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Argon or Carbon](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models); [Anthropic Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview); [OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra/Sol or GPT-6 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-selection). Example task entry: `AI · GPT-6.1 Terra · High`. Reasoning labels are tool-specific. Use [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models) for comparison when needed; project evidence takes priority.

Consider [TypeSafe Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/coding-agents), a decision model, for bounded categorization, routing, scoring and checks against supplied evidence when you need structured answers instead of generated text. Supply clear criteria, test representative cases and handle uncertain/no-match results; use code for exact calculations, generative models for writing and complex reasoning, and preserve existing approval authority.

Once a checklist has passed manual validation, implement its repeatable steps as a bounded LangGraph workflow only where automation suits the story, reusing [Gemini Fullstack LangGraph Quickstart](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-fullstack-langgraph-quickstart) scaffolding where it fits. Give each graph step inputs restricted to sanitized, fixed evidence, an explicit output, the existing check ID it serves, and this section's time, cost and retry bounds. Keep checks deterministic in code; a model node may only summarize approved evidence and never decides a check result. Record the graph as Automation and the model node as AI with its Model and Reasoning. Use the project's Gemini API key from approved secret storage when available. When it is unavailable, label any summary as manual with its author, mark checks that require a live Gemini call NOT RUN with the reason, and mark their step Blocked on the key. Keep manual steps wherever human verification is required. Also cap each whole run, for example with LangGraph's `recursion_limit`, and test reaching the cap: the run stops, keeps only results already verified with evidence, marks unreached checks NOT RUN and the step Blocked with the reason, and is not retried by raising the cap without a changed hypothesis. Pause and resume inside the graph, for example with a checkpointer backed `interrupt`, only where human input must arrive mid run; keep any stored state under the privacy rules. Otherwise end the run and hand off to the manual step.

**Reconcile → select one eligible step → execute → verify → record → recompute → repeat.** Eligibility requires validated inputs/dependencies, executor, authority and budget. Expand only the immediate step; keep later steps concise. Continue independent work only if pending decisions cannot invalidate it. Preserve completed contracts/results inline or by link before expanding the next step. A tool success or subagent report alone is not acceptance evidence.

For concurrency, use a coordinator or atomic shared claim: record step/files, executor, start and expected duration; read back the successful claim. Conflicting claimants wait. Without reliable coordination, use one writer for that scope. An overdue claim does not authorize takeover: establish that the prior executor stopped, inspect partial effects and record reassignment. Refresh before writeback; inspect uncertain writes before retry. Set proportionate time/cost/retry bounds and change the hypothesis before repeating failed attempts.

Check results: Pass (observed expected result with evidence), Fail (observed mismatch with evidence), NOT RUN (check not performed), or N/A — reason (check legitimately inapplicable). Missing knowledge is Pending with a reason, not N/A; a failed criterion cannot be retired this way. Human acceptance requirement is required, not required, or Pending with reason; its actual decision is Pending, accepted, or rejected, with source.

Step states: Pending; In progress (executor/time); Rework (executed check failed); Blocked (specific dependency); Complete (checks passed with evidence); N/A (irrelevant, with reason); Superseded (reason and existing replacement ID). Unknown is not N/A. Neither N/A nor Superseded retires a failed criterion. Evidence governs summaries; changed inputs/criteria reopen affected checks.

## Review and acceptance

Use the in-app browser, Chrome, or another browser, manually or through Playwright, as the intended end user. Verify the actual page layout, related lists, available actions, and visible data relevant to the journey. Record the entry point, user role, actions, expected behavior and observed result. Use MCP/CLI for backend checks on records, metadata, and supporting state. An inaccessible page or missing action leaves the dependent user journey unverified. Record human acceptance separately from test execution.

Check both human readability and AI execution precision; one reviewer may wear both hats, clearly labeled as maker review when applicable. Human-reader perspective is not human acceptance. A required independent checker must be fresh and inspect actual evidence against frozen criteria. Mockups/model opinions do not prove implementation.

For requested/needed review, send only permitted context: precise question, exact revision, criteria, relevant artifact/evidence, and bounded output structure. Ask for findings with location, impact, correction and verification. Record reviewer, model and reasoning, scope, findings, dispositions and affected rechecks; verify advice before acting. Reuse unchanged valid reviews. Access/model/transmission failures are blockers, not verdicts. Preserve required independent and human acceptance separately; do not invent approval gates or approvals.

For code changes, choose repeatable checks for the changed behavior and its material failure paths. Record the revision, runtime versions and observed results. Verify findings against agreed behavior and reproducible cases. Record confirmed defects and unresolved findings. Send policy questions to the decision owner before changing behavior. Review findings inform decisions. Passing checks require observed results. Where warranted, retain a regression test and rerun affected checks on the repaired revision. Check transaction, access and recovery boundaries touched by the change. Use measurements to support performance claims.

The story coordinator, assigned by the accountable human, uses the agreed criteria, risk and repository rules to decide what to check, when and who checks it. Plan this before implementation and revisit it when scope or risk changes. The accountable human owns acceptance policy, business decisions and any required release approval. For material changes to behavior, shared contracts, access, data or recovery, schedule a fresh independent reviewer after the writer's checks and before merge or handoff. Follow any stricter project requirements. Choose a human or an AI permitted by project policy and suited to the risk and context. Record the selected model and reasoning for an AI review. The reviewer inspects the proposed revision and evidence. Repairs reopen affected checks and findings.

**Code slice review.** Review each new or changed code slice before dependent work builds on it. Keep the slice the smallest coherent, testable unit and group its related edits. Prepare evidence with the repository command, local tests and dry runs as needed. Both reviews below are mandatory for code, in this order, with no substitute reviewer:

1. Run CodeRabbit on the proposed revision. Verify each finding, fix confirmed problems, rerun affected checks and rerun CodeRabbit on the changed scope.
2. Request the final review of the repaired revision from Claude Opus 5.5 in a fresh session that did not write the slice. Ask for only exact additions, deletions or refinements with file and line anchors, or a short statement that none are needed.
3. Apply confirmed Opus fixes and rerun affected checks. If those fixes require CodeRabbit to recheck the affected scope, request another Opus review of the rechecked revision, so Opus always gives the last review. Record both reviews against the final revision.

Proceed with dependent implementation, deployment, merge or handoff only after CodeRabbit and Opus have both completed their reviews, confirmed findings are fixed, and the affected rechecks pass. If either reviewer is unavailable, mark that review step Blocked with the reason and hold dependent work; unrelated work may continue. For code, the Opus review satisfies the fresh independent review above. Human acceptance stays separate.

**Pull requests and merge.** Work on a branch scoped to one story slice or one documentation change, and keep unrelated edits out. Change the default branch through a pull request unless authority already given permits a direct push, and record that source. Open the pull request as a draft while the writer's checks are incomplete. Record the exact revision for every check and review; a local check or CodeRabbit CLI review counts for the pull request only when it records the same revision as the PR head. If CodeRabbit runs through its GitHub App, mark the pull request ready for review before step 1 of the code slice review, because automatic reviewers may skip drafts; marking it ready does not grant merge permission. A push after a result makes that result historical for the changed scope, so rerun the affected checks and reviews on the new head. Keep technical evidence (the checks and reviews recorded against the final head), merge authority and business acceptance as separate records, because none of them implies another. Merge only with authority already given for that repository and branch, and record its source. Code still needs the code slice review before merge. For other changes, if that authority allows merging while evidence or acceptance is pending, list each pending item in the pull request and the story, and do not mark the affected steps Complete. Merging is not acceptance, and acceptance does not authorize a merge or deployment. Scale checks to the change: a change that alters no executable code follows the documentation row in [Code quality checks](../CODE-QUALITY.md) instead of the code slice review. A Salesforce change applies the code slice review to its code, runs the repository's tests and authorized validation against the target environment, and treats deployment as a separate authorized action. For optional repository settings, see the same guide.

Put applicable code checks behind a repository-owned command that works locally and in CI. The linked execution record identifies the check, executor and result. The story links the observed result to the relevant criterion. For examples and an optional Python workflow, see [Code quality checks](../CODE-QUALITY.md).

## Supporting detail when needed

For work exploring standard product capabilities through bounded experiments, read [OOTB discovery and experiments](../references/ootb-experiments.md) at this guide revision. Load it only when that approach is relevant; link the execution record from the story.

- **Design/research:** question and AC IDs; verified facts and dated/versioned source sections; approach/alternatives/tradeoffs; contracts/data flow and failure behavior; assumptions, decisions and validation plan.
- **Debugging:** expected/observed behavior, reproducible case/environment; logs, hypotheses and discriminating checks; diagnosis/confidence; exact fix reference; original-failure retest and affected regressions; limits/recovery. Mark hypotheses untested/supported/disproven. A successful command is not proof of a fix. Keep sensitive raw logs restricted.
- **Configuration:** required keys/types/defaults/validation, runtime/tool versions and retrieval mechanism. Commit placeholders/synthetic fixtures; keep real values outside the checkout where practical, otherwise verify local files are ignored and untracked. Use approved secret storage; never print secrets. Label proposed/unrun commands honestly.

See the [worked example](../EXAMPLE.md) for the current format and the [archive](../archive/README.md) for the prior format. [Validation history](../VALIDATION.md) documents earlier revisions.
